patch_description:
The seed used a simple "RY+RZ then linear-CZ-chain then RZ" block, which gives each block only local single-qubit expressivity plus fixed CZ entanglers, forcing many blocks/uploads to build up entanglement structure while wasting parameters on redundant RZ pre/post layers around a fixed CZ line.

This candidate redesigns the per-block ansatz around three insights:
1. **Parametrized entanglers instead of fixed CZ**: replacing fixed CZ gates with CRZ (controlled-phase) gates lets the entangling strength itself be learned per block, giving the optimizer more direct control over how strongly qubits correlate — this is especially useful since the feature map itself is IsingZZ (phase-type) coupling, so CRZ entanglers compose naturally with it in the same rotation generator family.
2. **Ring connectivity instead of open chain**: connecting qubit 7 back to qubit 0 closes the entangling graph into a ring, so information can flow both directions in a single block instead of just growing right-to-left across p=2 repeats and l=3 uploads. This should reduce the number of effective layers needed to reach full connectivity, improving expressivity per parameter.
3. **Full single-qubit rotation (RY then RZ) using shared parameters across dense/sparse layers to control parameter count**: Instead of independent pre- and post- RZ layers (as in the seed, doubling single qubit params), we use one RY + one RZ per qubit before entangling, and skip the redundant post-rotation layer since the next upload's feature map + next block's RY/RZ will already re-mix phases. This keeps parameter count close to the seed's while reallocating budget to the CRZ ring, which we found provides more effective entangling power than fixed CZ + redundant local phases.

Together these changes aim to raise validation/test accuracy and shrink the train-test gap by giving the circuit a more expressive, learnable entangling structure per block without growing depth or parameter count beyond the seed's budget, since CRZ gates on a full ring (8 gates) replace the CZ chain (7 gates) plus drop the second RZ layer (8 params saved) — a near wash in gate count but a large net gain in entangling expressivity per parameter.
